findings.reason: Verified that TotalDocs iterates b.cache with no lock while BuildIndex writes it, and the new init-time caller at search.go:216 runs right after the handleEvent goroutine starts, so the concurrent map read/write is newly reachable; the unlocked scrape path already existed, which limits the score.

Verified that the closure assigns the outer err from line 181 with `_, _, err = s.build(...)` and increments totalBatchesIndexed unsynchronised; the cacheMu lock that used to serialise builds was removed from BuildIndex, so the workers now overlap and a failed build can be lost when another worker overwrites err.

Verified that Stop's initErr assignments are no longer read because the handlers stopped calling Init, so requests are no longer refused after Stop, a real behaviour change, though the impact is limited since no caller of server.Stop exists inside pkg/storage/unified.
The background-derived ctx at server.go:229 is confirmed and Init now blocks the constructor, but the claim about shutdown during startup is a design concern whose severity was not shown concretely.

This is a question about whether the eager init caused the postgres CI failure; the skip with a TODO is visible in the test, but the causal link is unverified and the finding is phrased as a request to confirm.
